newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lukoil, ARCO, sign $5 billion oil joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Lukoil, ARCO, sign $5 billion oil joint venture.

text.p: Russia's NK LUKoil and the Atlantic Richfield Co. signed a $5 billion joint venture agreement in Moscow Thursday to undertake oil and gas projects in Russia and other countries, a LUKoil statement said.
It said that LUKoil, Russia's largest oil producer, had a 54 percent stake, while ARCO had a 46 percent stake. ARCO owns about 8 percent of LUKoil.

LUKoil spokesman Dmitry Dolgov said the signing followed the initialling of a cooperation agreement between the two sides in March, in which LUKoil said the two firms would invest $3 billion over a 10-year period in energy projects in the former Soviet Union.
"Then we were talking about $3 billion, now we're talking about $5 billion," Dolgov said.
The statement said most of the financing would come from ARCO.
No details were immediately available on which projects the venture, called LUKARCO, would undertake.

"The signing of the agreement is unprecedented in terms of cooperation between Russian and American oil companies, opens significant possibilities for joint activities and testifies to the growing confidence of Western investors in Russia's political stability and economic developments," LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov was quoted as saying.

"Work on identifying concrete investment projects has already begun, which will initiate the working phase of this entire project," the Russian-language release quoted ARCO Board Chairman Michael Bowlin as saying.
LUKoil is Russia's largest oil producer, with crude oil output last year of 57.3 million tons and 1995 net profits of about $528 million based on Russian accounting standards.
